proposals.before: He was soon promoted to left chief clerk of the Secretariat.
proposals.after: He was soon promoted to left chief clerk to the minister of education.
proposals.reason: Chinese 司徒 is the minister of education / director of instruction, not the Secretariat (中書).

proposals.before: When Emperor Xuan was regent he made Zhi left chief clerk of the Secretariat, retaining his general's title.
proposals.after: When Emperor Xuan was regent he made Zhi left chief clerk to the minister of education, retaining his general's title.
proposals.reason: Chinese 司徒左長史 is left chief clerk to the minister of education, not of the Secretariat.

proposals.before: When Yu Xiaoqing attacked Jin'an by sea, Shancai again went to Kuaiji in his existing office and directed the strategy.
proposals.after: When Yu Xiaoxu attacked Jin'an by sea, Shancai again went to Kuaiji in his existing office and directed the strategy.
proposals.reason: Chinese 余孝頃 is the same person earlier rendered Yu Xiaoxu; Xiaoqing is an inconsistent transliteration.

proposals.before: He then sent Zai's clansman Hui bearing a letter to explain to Zai the reason for executing Wang Sengbian, and also presented an edict of Emperor Jing of Liang, edict ordering Zai to disarm.
proposals.after: He then sent Zai's clansman Hui bearing a letter to explain to Zai the reason for executing Wang Sengbian, and also presented an edict of Emperor Jing of Liang ordering Zai to disarm.
proposals.reason: Literal English repeats 'edict' redundantly and obscures the single-command reading of 敕載解兵.

proposals.before: His grandfather Ai was Liang general who assists the state.
proposals.after: His grandfather Ai was Liang's General Who Assists the State.
proposals.reason: The office 輔國將軍 is a formal title and needs the definite title form plus a possessive/article so English does not read as a bare common noun phrase.

proposals.before: During Taijian he died in office and was posthumously presented as inspector of Ming, Huo, and Luo provinces.
proposals.after: During Taijian he died in office and was posthumously made inspector of Ming, Huo, and Luo provinces.
proposals.reason: 贈 marks posthumous conferral of office; English “presented as” misstates the appointment sense already rendered correctly in the idiomatic field.

decisions.reason: s0019 尋遷司徒左長史 names the office under 司徒 (minister of education / one of the Three Dukes), not the Secretariat (中書); “left chief clerk of the Secretariat” is a mistranslation, and the proposed replacement matches the Chinese.

s0122 以為司徒左長史 again has 司徒, not 中書; “left chief clerk of the Secretariat” is wrong, and “left chief clerk to the minister of education” correctly renders the office while keeping the regency and general-title clauses intact.
s0092 余孝頃 romanizes as Yu Xiaoqing (頃 = qǐng). Changing to Yu Xiaoxu would misread 頃 and introduce a naming error; consistency with another English spelling does not override the Chinese.

s0147 并奉梁敬帝敕，敕載解兵 is one edict that orders Zai to disarm; the literal’s bare second “edict” is broken English, and dropping the redundant noun keeps the letter, Jing’s edict, and the disarm order without adding or omitting content.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 并奉梁敬帝敕，敕載解兵

decisions.reason: s0162 梁輔國將軍 is the formal title 輔國將軍 under Liang; “Liang general who assists the state” reads as a bare common noun and is ungrammatical, while “Liang's General Who Assists the State” correctly titles the office.
s0173 贈明、霍、羅三州刺史 uses 贈 for posthumous conferral of office; “presented as” misstates that sense, and “posthumously made” matches the appointment meaning already used in the idiomatic field.
